research_question: In HIV-positive pregnant women, does daily cotrimoxazole prophylaxis (CTXp) combined with an additional antimalarial (mefloquine or dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine) reduce the risk of low birth weight (<2500 g) compared with CTXp alone (with or without placebo, current standard of care)?
treatment_label: Daily cotrimoxazole prophylaxis plus an additional antimalarial (mefloquine or dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine)
control_label: Daily cotrimoxazole prophylaxis alone, with or without placebo (standard of care)
outcome_description: Low birth weight, defined as a live-born infant weighing less than 2500 g at birth; extracted as the number of low-birth-weight events and the total number of women/infants randomized (or evaluated) per trial arm.
positive_direction: A positive effect (RR below 1 after signing) means the added antimalarial plus CTXp reduced the risk of low birth weight relative to CTXp alone — i.e. fewer low-birth-weight babies in the intervention arm.
search_queries: cotrimoxazole prophylaxis mefloquine HIV pregnant women randomized trial birth weight
dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine intermittent preventive treatment HIV pregnancy trial low birth weight
malaria chemoprevention HIV-infected pregnant women cotrimoxazole controlled trial birth outcomes
inclusion_criteria: Studies of pregnant women who are HIV-positive (or with an HIV-positive subgroup) receiving cotrimoxazole prophylaxis, in which an additional antimalarial (e.g. mefloquine, dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine, or similar chemoprevention) is compared with cotrimoxazole alone or cotrimoxazole plus placebo
Any controlled or comparative design (randomized, quasi-experimental, or controlled cohort) reporting at least one birth or pregnancy outcome
Reports quantitative data on birth weight or low birth weight (<2500 g), including event counts, proportions, means, or effect estimates
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, commentaries, opinion pieces, guidelines, or purely theoretical/modelling papers)
No comparison between a treatment arm and a control/standard-of-care arm (single-arm or purely descriptive studies)
No quantitative outcome data from which an effect size can be computed (no event counts/proportions, means+SDs, t/F values, or risk/odds ratios with uncertainty)
Completely unrelated to malaria chemoprevention or cotrimoxazole prophylaxis in HIV-positive pregnancy and birth outcomes
moderators_to_extract: Additional antimalarial agent used (mefloquine vs dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine vs other)
Use of placebo in the control arm (placebo-controlled vs open-label CTXp alone)
Sample size category and risk-of-bias rating
effect_size_note: Pool as a Risk Ratio using each trial's reported low-birth-weight event counts and total randomized (or evaluable) participants per arm, with a random-effects model; RR < 1 favours the added antimalarial.
